newsitem.title: TURKEY: Lead-up to Turkish PM Erbakan's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Lead-up to Turkish PM Erbakan's resignation.

text.p: Here is a chronology of the main events leading to the resignation on Wednesday of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan of the Islam-based Welfare Party.
December 24, 1995 - Welfare clinches narrow 21-percent plurality in general polls. Tansu Ciller's True Path Party runs third with 20 percent.
June 28, 1996 - Months of bargaining end with Erbakan and Ciller reaching coalition agreement.
July 8 - Islamist-led coalition wins confidence vote.
August 10 - Erbakan arrives in Iran on first foreign visit, calling for close ties with the neighbouring Islamic state.
August 12 - Turkey signs $23 billion gas deal with Iran to import gas through pipeline from Iran, despite U.S. protests.
October 6 - Erbakan visits Libya. Opposition outraged by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, who calls for creation of a Kurdish state. Erbakan later clears censure vote.
November 3 - Car containing government MP, police chief and crime boss crashes, sparking scandal over state-mafia links.
November 8 - Interior Minister Mehmet Agar of True Path Party resigns over widening car crash scandal.
December 1 - Turkey confirms defence pact with Israel, despite Erbakan's pre-election promises to scrap the deal.

January 10, 1997 - Holy month of Ramadan starts in most of Moslem world. Welfare promotes Islamist agenda all month, saying it will lift headscarf ban in public workplaces and build mosques in secularist strongholds.
January 31 - Welfare mayor calls for Islamic law at Islamist protest in Ankara's Sincan district attended by Iranian envoy.
February 1 - Beginning of nightly anti-government protests.
February 4 - Tanks parade through Sincan, in thinly-veiled military warning to Erbakan's Welfare Party.
February 25 - Coalition clears second censure motion.
February 28 - The military-dominated National Security Council demands a government crackdown on religious extremism.
April 4 - Parliament commission investigating state-gangland ties accuses two government MPs of involvement.
April 26 - Two conservative ministers resign in protest against government's refusal to implement anti-Islamist campaign. They begin search for new coalition formula.
April 26 - Army uses monthly National Security Council meeting to renew demands for curb on Islamist activism.
May 11 - Tens of thousands of Islamists rally in Istanbul to protest against planned closing of Koranic schools.
May 17 - Third conservative minister quits government, saying she backs effort to end Islamist rule.
May 19 - MP from ruling Welfare Party resigns and joins main opposition Motherland Party, bringing government's total of deputies -- on paper -- to 280 out of 550 seats.
May 20 - Government survives fourth censure motion.
May 21 - Chief prosecutor opens case to close Welfare.
May 22 - Erbakan says he will sue the chief prosecutor.
May 30 - The government loses its absolute majority in parliament as a former minister resigns from True Path to follow other defectors.
June 1 - Erbakan and Ciller call for early elections.
June 11 - True Path decides to withdraw from the government unless Ciller is made prime minister by June 18.
June 12 - A Welfare party MP resigns leaving government in a minority in parliament.
June 13 - The True Path tourism minister quits the cabinet.
June 16 - Erbakan talks of power handover to Ciller, but sets no date. Welfare MPs say there are conditions attached.
June 16 - Ciller says the coalition will end "in one or two days".
June 18 - Two radical Welfare MPs quit the party.
June 18 - Erbakan announces resignation and seeks President Demirel's approval for revamped coalition plan.
